Four products, one codebase, one tag. Every release ships all four in
lockstep, same version, each with its own image, its own Helm chart and its own
Podman Quadlet units. Pick the one that fits the box. Every product speaks
every protocol HotLoop has, so you never step up a product just to read the
PLC on your bench. Features split them. Protocols don't.

| <span class="sr-only">Details</span> | HotLoop IoT | HotLoop Edge | HotLoop Gateway | HotLoop Edge Relay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| What it's for | The automation base. A Pi, a NUC, a box in a closet | A box at the machine, with the uplink allowed to die | The site brain | Poll, forward, survive. No database, no UI |
| Entities, automations, helpers, scripts, recipes, blueprints, dashboards, logbook, notifications, MCP, MQTT with discovery, ISA-18.2 alarms, backups, every driver | yes | yes | yes | drivers only |
| OPC UA server, Sparkplug edge publishing with store and forward | | yes | yes | publishing only |
| Fleet, multi-site, scheduled reports | | | yes | |
| Image | `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop-iot` | `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop-edge` | `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop` | `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop-edge-relay` |
| Chart | `hotloop-iot` | `hotloop-edge` | `hotloop` | `hotloop-edge-relay` |
| Quadlet units | `deploy/quadlet/iot/` | `deploy/quadlet/edge/` | `deploy/quadlet/gateway/` | `deploy/quadlet/edge-relay.container` |
| Quadlet units on SQLite | `deploy/quadlet/iot/sqlite/` | `deploy/quadlet/edge/sqlite/` | `deploy/quadlet/gateway/sqlite/` | none |
| `database.type` in the chart | `postgresql` (default), `sqlite` | `timescaledb` (default), `postgresql`, `sqlite` | `timescaledb` (default), `postgresql`, `sqlite` | none |
| Architectures | amd64, arm64, arm/v7 | amd64, arm64, arm/v7 | amd64, arm64 | amd64, arm64, arm/v7 |
| Database the chart and Quadlet run | PostgreSQL 16 | TimescaleDB | TimescaleDB | none |
| History kept by default | 30 days | 90 days | 90 days | none |
| Databases the binary runs on | SQLite or Postgres | SQLite, Postgres or TimescaleDB | SQLite, Postgres or TimescaleDB | none |

The database is a setting, not an image: `HOTLOOP_DB_TYPE=sqlite` and
`HOTLOOP_DB_PATH` put any of the three on a SQLite file with no database
container at all (DEPLOYMENT.md, "SQLite"). The charts take the same choice as
`database.type` and the Quadlet units as the `sqlite/` directories, each product
offering only the databases in the table above: asking the IoT chart for
`timescaledb` fails the install. Moving from one database to another is a
backup and a restore (BACKUP.md).

The Gateway kept the names it shipped under through 4.17.0: image
`ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop`, chart `hotloop`. Nobody running it has to change
a thing.

## What's in a product is what's in the binary

A product is a build, not a setting. `-tags hotloop_iot` builds IoT,
`-tags hotloop_edge` builds Edge, no tag builds the Gateway. What a product
doesn't have isn't switched off, it isn't there: the OPC UA server isn't in the
IoT image at all, so no environment variable, no values file and no bad day can
turn it on. `internal/product/packages.go` says which product links which
package, and the suite fails the moment a binary links something it shouldn't.

So a smaller product answers for what it doesn't have instead of pretending:

- **The API** keeps every route in every product. A route for a feature this
  product doesn't have answers `404` and names the product that does:
  `{"error":"scheduled reports are part of HotLoop Gateway; this is HotLoop IoT","product":"iot","feature":"reports"}`.
  `GET /api/status` says `product` and `features`, so a script asks instead of
  probing.
- **A Gateway-only setting** on IoT or Edge (`HOTLOOP_REPORTS_ENABLED=true`
  carried down in an old values file, say) warns at startup and on the Settings
  screen, and HotLoop runs. Refusing to start a plant over a report nobody can
  get is stupid, and ignoring it silently is how nobody notices for a month.
- **The charts** don't have the setting at all. `charts/hotloop-iot` has no
  `reports`, `opcuaServer` or `edgePublish` block, and `hotloop-edge` has no
  `reports`. Set one anyway and it renders nothing.
- **`hotloop --product`** prints `iot`, `edge` or `gateway`. `--version` still
  prints only the version, because scripts parse it.

## Which one

- **A Pi, smart plugs, a few sensors, an MQTT broker full of Tasmota and
  Zigbee2MQTT, or one PLC on a bench:** IoT. It's the smallest image (about 29
  MB on arm) and plain PostgreSQL's image is a sixth of TimescaleDB's, which on
  an SD card is the number that matters.
- **A box bolted next to a line, feeding SCADA over OPC UA, or publishing
  upstream over Sparkplug and riding out the uplink going down:** Edge.
- **The site: every line, reports mailed on a schedule, edge relays reporting
  in, more than one site on one screen:** Gateway.
- **A box that should poll and forward and nothing else, with no database to
  look after:** Edge Relay. See [EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/).

## Sizes

Measured from images built from this repository's Containerfiles with Podman,
stripped static binaries on distroless/static. The image is the binary plus
about 3 MB of base.

| <span class="sr-only">Details</span> | amd64 image / binary | arm64 image / binary | arm/v7 image / binary |
|---|---|---|---|
| IoT | 31.2 / 28.0 MB | 29.1 / 26.0 MB | 29.2 / 26.0 MB |
| Edge | 36.5 / 33.3 MB | 34.2 / 31.0 MB | 34.3 / 31.1 MB |
| Gateway | 37.1 / 33.9 MB | 34.8 / 31.6 MB | not built |
| Edge Relay | 15.7 / 12.5 MB | 14.9 / 11.7 MB | 15.1 / 11.9 MB |

Those are on disk. What a product uses running, with devices polling on a real
Pi, hasn't been measured yet: idle with no devices, HotLoop sits around 10 MB
of RSS and PostgreSQL around 12 MB, and that's the floor, not the number.

## Installing

### Helm

One repository, all four charts:

```sh
helm repo add hotloop https://hotloop.io/hotloop/

helm install hotloop hotloop/hotloop-iot  --namespace hotloop --create-namespace
helm install hotloop hotloop/hotloop-edge --namespace hotloop --create-namespace
helm install hotloop hotloop/hotloop      --namespace hotloop --create-namespace
```

Call the release `hotloop` whichever product it is. The release name is what
the database's volume, the Secrets and the Service are named after, and keeping
it is what lets a site move up a product later (below).

On EmberNET, each one is its own card in the App Store: "HotLoop IoT", "HotLoop
Edge", "HotLoop Gateway" and "HotLoop Edge Relay". A store deploy folds the
dashboard's tenant labels into everything the chart renders, and Running Apps
shows them as `HotLoop-IoT`, `HotLoop-Edge`, `HotLoop-Gateway` and
`HotLoop-Edge-Relay`.

### Podman Quadlet

For a box that isn't in a cluster. Each product directory under
`deploy/quadlet/` has five units: `hotloop.network`, `hotloop.container` (the app),
`hotloop-db.container` (its database, the same image and version its chart
runs), `hotloop-db.volume` and `hotloop-data.volume`. The install steps are in
the header of each `hotloop.container`, and
[deploy/quadlet/README.md](/install/quadlet/) has the rest.

These need Podman 5.0 or newer. Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm ships 4.3,
which has no Quadlet at all, so a Pi wants Raspberry Pi OS Trixie or newer. The
app follows `:stable` and Podman's auto-update moves it, with the database
pinned: [the Quadlet README](/install/auto-update/) has how and why.
Whichever way it's installed, put the database on a USB SSD and not the SD
card. History writes all day, every day, and SD cards die of exactly that.

## Moving a site up a product

IoT to Edge to the Gateway keeps every device, tag, entity, automation, alarm,
user and hour of history. Every product runs every migration, so the database
is the same shape in all three, and the bigger product starts with its extra
features empty.

- **Quadlet:** the unit names, the volumes and the secrets are the same in
  every product directory. Copy the bigger product's `hotloop.container` and
  `hotloop-db.container` over yours, `systemctl daemon-reload`, restart.
- **Helm:** `helm upgrade hotloop hotloop/hotloop-edge` (or `hotloop/hotloop`)
  on the same release. The three charts select their pods with the same
  labels and name the database's StatefulSet and volume the same, so the
  upgrade is allowed and the volume stays bound.

Take a backup first (`POST /api/backup`, see [BACKUP.md](/iot/backup/)) and copy it
off the box. What's been run: the Quadlet units, IoT then Edge then the Gateway,
one database volume, the same device there at every step, and the IoT
database's PostgreSQL 16 directory starting under the Gateway's TimescaleDB
image. History stays in native partitions after that move; a hypertable takes a
backup and a restore into a fresh TimescaleDB. What hasn't been run yet: the
same move as a `helm upgrade` on a real cluster, and going back down a product.
Don't take a box you care about down a product until it has been.

## How they ship

One `v` tag releases all four. RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md
has the steps; the short version:

- `.github/scripts/release_guard.sh X.Y.Z` checks every chart's version, every
  chart's image, that every Quadlet app unit follows `:stable` with a healthcheck, and every database unit matches its chart and is never auto-updated, that the IoT
  and Edge charts match their generator, and renders every chart the way a hand
  install and the App Store deploy it. `release.yml` runs it before anything
  builds, and it runs the same on a laptop.
- One Containerfile builds IoT, Edge and the Gateway, with `PRODUCT` picking the
  build tag. The build asks the binary `--product` and fails if it's wrong.
  `Containerfile.edge-relay` builds the relay.
- `charts/hotloop-iot` and `charts/hotloop-edge` are generated from
  `charts/hotloop` by `.github/scripts/make_product_charts.py` and committed.
  Edit the Gateway chart, rerun it, commit all three. A part of a template
  only some products have sits between `product:` and `end product` marker
  comments; the generator keeps or drops it per product and refuses a
  template that reads a setting its product doesn't have.
